Global cotton production is forecast to decline 4 per cent in 2026-27 to 25.75 million tonnes, while consumption is expected to rise 0.8 per cent to 26.1 million tonnes, creating a projected supply deficit of 353,000 tonnes, ICAC said.

title: Australian wool market shows signs of stabilisation in November
summary:
Australia's wool market eased for a fourth week, with the EMI down 25 cents to 1,698 Auc/kg and 21 cents lower in US-dollar terms.
Australian Wool Innovation said 25,022 bales were offered, 21,618 sold and the pass-in rate halved to 13.6 per cent.
Superfine clearances improved, but crossbred indicators stayed under pressure ahead of a 30,919-bale Week 20 forecast.

title: US cotton export sales rise 28%, but shipments hit to year low
summary:
US Upland cotton net sales rose 28 per cent to 277,500 RB in the week ended October 29, 53 per cent above the four-week average, with Vietnam the top buyer at 200,500 RB.
Upland shipments fell 14 per cent to a marketing-year low of 137,800 RB.
Pima sales rebounded to 6,400 RB, led by India, while shipments more than doubled from 3,300 RB to 7,100 RB.

title: Hyosung TNC profit jumps 97%, but can bio-spandex transform its future
summary:

Operating profit was KRW 110.2 billion, up 96.7 per cent year on year but 41.6 per cent lower sequentially; nine-month profit rose 86.3 per cent.
Spandex volumes fell after Q2 restocking, prices stayed flat and brands can assess certified lower-carbon spandex.

title: Global cotton faces a 353,000-tonne deficit: Why are prices falling?
summary:
Projected 2027 global cotton deficits mask swelling Chinese stocks, weak yarn movement and price pressure, leaving mills exposed to sourcing risks.
ICAC sees a 353,000-tonne 2026-27 deficit, while USDA estimates 1.12 million tonnes, but global ending stocks remain near 15.39 million tonnes.
TexPro shows China’s yarn imports rising as Brazil exports grow and India and Pakistan import more cotton.

title: Drewry WCI further down, congestion eased on Chinese ports
summary:
Drewry’s World Container Index fell 1 per cent to $4,389 per FEU in the week ending November 5 as Transpacific and Asia–Europe routes weakened.
Shanghai–New York rates dropped 3 per cent, Shanghai–Rotterdam slipped 2 per cent and Chinese port waiting times eased.
Drewry sees downward pressure as effective capacity rises, Suez Canal transits increase and demand stays weak.

title: ICE cotton futures extend gains on strong US export sales
summary:
ICE cotton futures rose for a second session as December 2026 settled 0.77 per cent higher at 78.71 cents per pound.
Gains were supported by strong US export sales, a weaker dollar and higher crude oil prices, which can lift polyester costs.
USDA said upland sales rose 28 per cent to 277,522 bales; China sales were just 87 bales, and resistance is near 79.06–80.00 cents.

title: Turkiye outlines 2027 roadmap to expand preferential trade network
summary:
Turkiye's 2027 trade roadmap aims to expand preferential trade ties, diversify export markets and strengthen global value chain integration. 
Plans include reactivating its FTA with Syria, advancing negotiations with Canada, Japan and the GCC, and pursuing talks with Algeria and Indonesia. 
The programme also prioritises green supply chains with the EU, digital trade infrastructure and export promotion.

summary:

TexPro shows US raw cotton sales to Vietnam at $1.51 billion versus Brazil’s $623 million, while Brazil led in China and Bangladesh.
A $75-per-tonne customs discount for Brazil is tempered by quality, freight, finance and Santos port risks.

title: Bangladesh's BRAC Bank cuts export document processing to one day
summary:
BRAC Bank completed Bangladesh’s first fully digital, end-to-end export documentary collection for a garment shipment to the UK, cutting document processing time from 40 days to one using blockchain technology and electronic trade documents. 
The transaction involved NAZ Bangladesh, Matalan and Lloyds Bank, the bank said.

summary:

summary:

The four technologies are Dri-FIT for dryness, Aero-FIT for cooling, Therma-FIT for warmth and Storm-FIT for protection from the elements across sports and changing running conditions.

Earlier gas and power shortages cut daily gas supply by 450–500 million cubic feet and caused 30–40 per cent production-capacity losses.
A six-member wage board aims to set revised pay by December 2026, with new wages to be paid in January 2027.

summary:
University of Memphis pilot findings suggest fabric type may affect microplastic levels in the personal breathing zone, with polyester T-shirts raising exposure by up to 42 per cent over cotton.
The study involved 10 participants wearing cotton and polyester-containing T-shirts, plus 12-hour bedroom baseline air measurements.
PET was found among 99 per cent of detected airborne microplastics.

title: Bangladesh garment crisis: Can 690 factories regain buyer confidence?
summary:

Workers seek a Tk 30,000 (~$241), monthly minimum, up from Tk 12,500; a revised scale is due from December but no amount is agreed.
Exports fell 1.64 per cent in fiscal 2025-26, while TexPro shows pressure in US-bound T-shirts and men’s woven clothing.
